english.title: Publish / cause another to publish statement intending / reckless as to encouragement of terrorism - Terrorism Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[published]_
(B)_[caused another to publish]_

a statement that was likely to be understood by some or all of the members of the public to whom it was published as a direct or indirect encouragement or other inducement to them to the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism or Convention offences and at the time when you

(C)_[published it]_
(D)_[caused it to be published]_

you intended members of the public to be or were reckless as to whether they would be directly or indirectly encouraged or otherwise induced by the statement to commit, prepare or instigate acts of terrorism or Convention offences
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1 of the Terrorism Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 1(3) of the Terrorism Act 2006 provides an interpretation of which statements are likely to encourage terrorism, including statements which glorify the commission/preparation of such acts/offences and are statements from which members of the public could reasonably expect to infer that what is being glorified is being glorified as conduct that should be emulated by them in existing circumstances.
(ii) Section 1(4) of the Act provides that the contents of the statement as a whole as well as the circumstances and manner of its publication must be considered.
(iii) Section 1(5) of the Act provides that it is irrelevant whether the encouragement relates to specific acts of terrorism/Convention offences or to such acts/offences generally and whether anybody is in fact encouraged/induced by the statement.
(iv) Section 1(6) of the Act provides a defence in cases where the offender acted recklessly if he shows that the statement neither expressed his views nor had his endorsement (but see section 3 of the Act) AND that it was clear, in all the circumstances of the statement's publication, that it did not express his views or have his endorsement.
(v) For the application of this section to internet activity etc. see section 3 of the Act.
(vi) This offence applies to acts done outside the United Kingdom regardless of the nationality of the offender, see section 17 of the Act.
(vii) For the liability of company directors etc. see section 18 of the Act.
(viii) Proceedings for this offence require the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, section 19 of the Act.
(ix) See Home Office Circular 8/2006, including explanations about this section.
(x) The penalty on indictment was increased to include a maximum of 15 years imprisonment from 12 April 2019; for offences from that date, please see document H20005.

other.powersofarrest:

Also applicable: Arrest without warrant
other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 7 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty is imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
